slot.brief: In a binomial expansion, find r so that two consecutive binomial coefficients are equal (n even/odd cases).

stem: For $(1+x)^n$, the coefficients of $x^r$ and $x^{r+1}$ are equal. Which condition must hold?

verdicts.working: Set \(\binom nr=\binom n{r+1}\). Then \(n-r=r+1\), so \(r=(n-1)/2\), which is an integer when \(n\) is odd.

working:
$\dfrac{C(n,r+1)}{C(n,r)}=\dfrac{n-r}{r+1}=1 \Rightarrow r=\dfrac{n-1}{2}$. For $r$ to be an integer, $n$ must be odd.

Independent check: Set \(\binom nr=\binom n{r+1}\). Then \(n-r=r+1\), so \(r=(n-1)/2\), which is an integer when \(n\) is odd.
